title: Soft-anchoring: weighted throughput guarantees and graceful spillover for regional dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Customers that reserve regional dedicated capacity want predictable throughput guarantees without hard binding to a single zone, while still honoring legal or contractual data residency constraints. Current placement approaches either (a) fully pin capacity to a zone (rigid, wasteful) or (b) treat regions as completely fungible (risky for residency-sensitive customers). We need a model that provides measurable per-customer throughput guarantees and fast, safe failover behavior across zones inside a region, while preserving data residency constraints for sensitive workloads.

Goal: Design and implement a 'soft-anchoring' placement policy and the associated autoscaling/failover machinery. Soft-anchoring provides a weighted reservation across multiple zones (an anchor profile), enforces data-residency tag constraints, exposes predictable throughput guarantees in the Console and API, and supports progressive spillover with TTL-based residency leases and quota fencing to avoid noisy neighbor amplification during failures.

Scope: This ticket covers the design spec, API surface (new fields for ReserveCapacity and FleetPolicy), runtime placement decisions, and rollout plan for Canary -> Gradual -> GA. Implementation work includes scheduler changes, eviction/failover orchestration hooks, metrics, and Console UX changes for contract visualization.
acceptance_criteria: API: ReserveCapacity supports anchor_profile field with zone weights and residency_tags; validation returns clear errors for conflicting constraints
Scheduler: Placement engine honors anchor_profile weights in steady state and migrates only when capacity or policy changes require it

Failover: Under partial zone failure, traffic is progressively spilled to other zones according to weights and pre-configured spill thresholds; request routing falls back under 200ms SLA for regional customers
Residency: Workloads with strict residency_tags must not be placed outside permitted zones; leases prevent placement into non-resident zones during transient state
Autoscaling: Autoscaler respects per-customer throughput guarantees and scale-to-empty rules when soft-anchored capacity is idle
Telemetry: Console shows reserved versus actual throughput, utilization per anchor slice, and incidents where spillover occurred
Safety: Chaos tests demonstrate no greater than 5% P99 latency regression for stable traffic during single-zone drain in canary runs
implementation_notes: Introduce 'anchor_profile' proto: list of {zone, weight, min_capacity, max_capacity, residency_tags}
Scheduler: add weighted placement pass after affinity ranking; maintain per-reservation state in PlacementStore with lease TTLs
Failover orchestration: implement progressive spill steps (soft->moderate->hard) with rate-limited re-routing and kv-cache warming hints
Quota fencing: add per-reservation kill switches to prevent runaway overcommit when multiple reservations attempt spillover simultaneously
Autoscaler: include reservation-aware scaling targets; when reserved_capacity > actual_demand, scale-down must honor min_capacity for anchor slices
Console: new Reserved Capacity view with anchor visualization, spillover audit log and suggested remediations
E2E tests: simulate zone latency/jitter, partial GPU failures, and cross-zone bandwidth constraints; create benchmark harness using small and large request footprints
risks: Cross-zone bandwidth costs could increase during sustained spillover if many customers opt-in to high weights in other zones
Lease TTL tuning: too short -> frequent flapping; too long -> slow recovery; needs careful calibration
Complexity of quota fencing with preexisting autoscale rules may cause inadvertent under-provisioning
Edge cases where residency constraints conflict with required min_capacity for an anchor slice will require clear error semantics and potential trade-offs (e.g., reduce weight vs deny request)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Internal alpha: enable feature only for infra test accounts and internal customers; monitor metrics and SLOs
Phase 1 - Select customers: invite 3 existing dedicated customers with diverse residency requirements; run guided migrations and gather feedback
Phase 2 - Gradual rollout: expose in Console with default conservative weights and soft-spill thresholds; add telemetry dashboards and alerting rules
Phase 3 - GA: enable API for self-serve reservations with quota checks and billing note about cross-zone egress/costs
metrics_and_alerting: Reserved throughput vs consumed throughput (per reservation) - gauge
Spillover fraction (requests redirected across zones) - rate
P99 latency delta during spillover windows - distribution
Number of failed placement attempts due to residency constraints - counter
Lease renewals per reservation (indicative of flapping) - rate
Alert: spillover fraction > 10% and sustained > 5 minutes -> pager for reliability oncall
